query: Create an evolutionary loop to optimize the branch predictor for a branch-intensive workload. STRICT REQUIREMENT: You MUST include 'champsim' in the tools_used array and map it correctly in the simulation node.

generated_loop.name: Evolutionary Branch Predictor Optimization Loop
generated_loop.description: An evolutionary loop that iteratively generates, simulates, evaluates, and evolves branch predictor configurations using ChampSim to maximize IPC for a branch‑intensive workload.

nodes.description: Initialize loop state with empty population and iteration counter
Generate initial random population of branch predictor configurations
Run ChampSim simulation for each configuration in the population
Extract IPC and other performance metrics from ChampSim output
Update best_ipc and best configuration in the loop state
Increment the iteration counter after each generation
Apply evolutionary operators (mutation, crossover) to generate next generation
Determine whether to continue evolution or finish
Emit the final best branch predictor configuration and its IPC

2.6 Branch Predictor Improvements 28
In gem5, multiple branch prediction models are available, many of
which were added since the initial release of gem5. Currently, gem5
supports five different branch prediction techniques including the
well-known TAGE predictor as well as standard predictors such as
bi-mode, tournament, etc. This list can easily be expanded to cover
different variants of these well-known branch predictors. Besides,
the support for loop predictor and indirect branch predictor is also
available.

5.4.2 “Classic” evolutionary discovery flows in CHIA.First, we look
at the design of an illustrative CHIA loop implementing an evo-
lutionary flow similar to the one seen in ArchAgent. In order to
do this, we provide ChampSim nodes and an AlphaEvolve node in
CHIA, organizing them as shown in Figure 12.
The user selects configurations for the ChampSim nodes, config-
uring the simulated SoC, and the AlphaEvolve node, configuring
various evolutionary search parameters. The user also provides a
few lightweight Python functions. The function build_fn is used
to define how binaries are built on a ChampSim Build node and built
binaries are passed further into evaluation. In the case of evolution
feedback, for example, ChampSim Run nodes could be set up to
execute a selection of workload traces from a workloads database
executing for a short number of warmup and detailed simulation
